There are no top-level commands, `exec`, `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or other dangerous constructs that would execute during sourcing. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.

The only parameter expansions at the top level are `${pkgname%-git}` and `${pkgver%%.r*}`, which are pure string manipulations producing `axolotl-apclient` and `0.1.6` respectively -- no command substitution, no `eval`, no shell execution. The `source` array references the project's own GitHub upstream and its known bundled third-party dependencies (imgui, IXWebSocket, sol2, lua), all recorded as data only, not executed at sourcing time. All `sha256sums` are `SKIP`, which is expected and harmless for this gate. No evidence of obfuscation, encoded payloads, or unexpected behavior in the top-level scope.
</details>
